card.ch2.title: The Missing Page
end.ch2.title: End of Chapter 2
end.ch2.body: The bridge holds, page 7 is (almost) whole, and a pencil owes you a favour. Or the other way round.

page.p5.title: The wind
page.p5.intro: In GRAND ADVENTURE DELUXE the wind blows realistically thanks to RealWind™ technology. Where natural wind cannot reach, we recommend the accessory below.
page.p5.cap: Fig. 3 — Pocket fan (do not point at the Narrator)
page.p5.note: The fan is not a toy. It is an accessory. The difference is the price.
page.p6.title: Recommended views
page.p6.intro: The Scenic Ravine is the pride of GRAND ADVENTURE DELUXE. Admire it from a safe distance and do not look down.
page.p6.cap: Fig. 6 — The Scenic Ravine. Width: 8 metres.
page.p7.title: How to cross the bridge
page.p7.torn: This page has been torn out. The missing pieces are elsewhere.
page.p7.a: 1. Walk to the edge of the Scenic Ravine.
page.p7.b: 2. Check that the bridge is as long as the ravine.
page.p7.c: 3. Cross. Do not look down (see p. 6).
page.p7.note: Bridge measurements are approximate. Doing the maths is the buyer's responsibility.
page.p7.margin: 3 metres? and how wide is the ravine?
page.p8.title: Notes
page.p8.intro: This page is reserved for your notes.
page.p8.margin: the page number is stuck on with spit
n.r1: Here we are: the Scenic Ravine. Lovely, isn't it? Shame about the bridge.
n.r2: Someone... corrected it. I'm naming no names. It was white and sticky.
n.r3: Don't panic: the manual explains how to cross. Page 7. Look.
n.r5: Fine. The pieces can't be far. Pages don't fly.
n.empty1: That's the sky. Courtesy of the background.
n.empty2: No page pieces there. I checked. More or less.
n.empty3: The ravine is staring at you. Don't stare back.
n.dropwrong1: And what exactly is that supposed to do?
n.tree1: A paper plane, stuck in the branches. It has printed lines on it. Suspicious.
n.tree2: Climbing is not covered by the manual. Ladders are in chapter 3.
n.tree3: You could blow. Very hard. For about a week.
n.tree_done: A tree. Now plane-free. Go back to being a tree.
n.fan1: A pocket fan aimed at a tree. Genius or vandalism, I haven't decided yet.
n.fan2: Wait. That plane is folded from a piece of page 7!
n.plaque_done1: The plaque. Very nice. The lecture is suspended due to audience rudeness.
n.plaque_done2: I'm not telling you anything else. You'd only move me.
n.lec1: Ah, the plaque! Let me tell you the history of the Scenic Ravine.
n.lec2: It all began in 1996, when an artist drew two rocks slightly too far apart.
n.lec3: The bridge came later. So did this plaque. I wrote it myself. By hand.
n.lec4: Note the typeface. Note the frame. Note the masterful use of the word 'scenic'.
n.lec5: ...Are you listening? Why are you looking under my box?
n.lec_end: End of lecture. There will be a quiz. Maybe.
n.grab2: ...There was a piece of page under me? Since when?
n.grab3: Fine, take it. But we're finishing the lecture another time. With slides.
n.ear1: That's a dog-ear. You don't dog-ear books. And you certainly don't un-dog-ear them.
n.ear2: You unfolded it. And inside there was... a piece of page 7. Of course there was.
n.ear_done: It's unfolded now. The damage is done.
n.more: A piece of page 7! Some pieces are still missing. Check the manual.
n.pg1: Page 7! Whole again! More or less. There's some tape.
n.pg2: "The bridge is 3 metres long." See? All you had to do was read.
n.pg4: The ravine is eight wide. I did the maths: five metres short. Roughly.
n.pg5: Never mind. They're just numbers. And numbers, unlike words, don't move.
n.gap1: There was a bridge here. Now there's a label. The Proofreader was... thorough.
n.gap2: Don't jump. This is not a platformer. Not yet.
n.short1: Three metres out of eight. The bridge is doing its best. It isn't enough.
n.short2: If you step on it, you fall. If you fall, we start over. If we start over, I give the lecture again.
n.long1: Eight metres?! Who changed the number?
n.long2: And why does the bottom of page 8 now say 3? There are two page 3s!
n.long3: The printer will find out. The printer ALWAYS finds out.
n.wow: "The bridge is BREATHTAKING metres long." The bridge doesn't know how long to be, so it's staying put.
n.rshort: Three metres again. You like living dangerously.
n.page_wow: Page BREATHTAKING. Finally a page number with some personality.
n.view_eight: "View: 8." Out of ten, I suppose. Harsh but fair.
n.cross1: Exactly eight metres. Fine, cross. Slowly. And don't look down.
p.1: nice trick with the page number.
n.p1: Who said that? Who's in the margin?
p.2: a pencil. the hints one. nice to meet you.
p.3: i can help you reach the end of the manual. in exchange for a small favour.
n.p3: We do NOT make deals with strange pencils! It says so on page... on some page.
n.p4: Let's move on. And you, pencil, stay in the margin.
n.flee1: The hints button? I've moved it somewhere safer. For you.
n.flee2: Yes, you can still see it. But it's on the left now. Nobody ever looks left.
n.typo_sign: "Brigde". The letters are all there. Just not in that order.
n.typo_exit: "Eixt". The Proofreader must have shuffled it. Or I did. Let's say the Proofreader.
n.typo_done: Yes, yes, you already found that one. Stop rubbing it in.
h.plane.1: That paper plane isn't just any paper: it has the lines of a printed page.
h.plane.2: You need a good gust of wind. The manual has a whole page about wind.
h.plane.3: Drag the fan from page 5 of the manual onto the tree.
h.lecture.1: The Narrator loves that plaque. Let him talk.
h.lecture.2: While he talks, look at the top edge of his box: something is under it.
h.lecture.3: Tap the plaque and, during the lecture, drag the Narrator's box upwards.
h.ear.1: On page 6 a corner is folded. People who fold pages always have something to hide.
h.ear.2: The Narrator says not to touch it. The Narrator says a lot of things.
h.ear.3: Tap the folded corner at the top of page 6 twice.
h.bridge.1: Three metres of bridge, eight of ravine. The problem is a number.
h.bridge.2: Crooked words come loose. So do numbers. Even the ones at the bottom of pages.
h.bridge.3: Drag the 8 from page 8's page number onto the 3 in the rule on page 7: hold the word over the manual's arrow to turn the page. Then tap the bridge.
h.none: No ideas right now. Odd: I usually have too many.
